```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Load required libraries
# tidyverse covers data manipulation (dplyr, stringr, readr, tidyr, purrr, lubridate)
library(tidyverse)

# Network analysis and visualization
library(igraph)      # core network analysis
library(tidygraph)   # tidy framework for network data
library(ggraph)      # network visualization
library(graphlayouts) # additional network layout algorithms
```

```{r}
# Load the public dataset from the working directory
# This file serves as the basis for all subsequent files in this repository
  PublicDF <- read_csv("PublicDF.csv",
                       col_types = cols(.default = "c", Volumen = "i", Expediente = "i"))
```

```{r build-edges-undirected}
# Build an undirected edge list from PublicDF
# Edges represent social connections documented in marriage applications:
# - Bride to Groom
# - Witnesses to Bride, Groom, or both depending on the For column
#   (Role = "B", "G", "W1", "W2", ...; For = "Bride", "Groom", "Both", or "N/A")

# Step 1: Sort within each wedding: Groom, Bride, then witnesses numerically (W1, W2, ... W10)
PublicDF <- PublicDF %>%
  mutate(RoleOrder = case_when(
    Role == "G" ~ 0,
    Role == "B" ~ 1,
    grepl("^W", Role) ~ 1 + as.numeric(gsub("\\D", "", Role)),
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  )) %>%
  arrange(WeddingID, RoleOrder)

# Any role the ranking didn't recognize? (should return nothing)
PublicDF %>% filter(is.na(RoleOrder)) %>% distinct(Role)

# Step 2: Helper to build sorted Source/Target pairs for one wedding
make_pair <- function(a, b, wed) {
  if (length(a) == 0 || length(b) == 0) return(NULL)
  expand.grid(a = a, b = b, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    transmute(Source = pmin(a, b), Target = pmax(a, b), WeddingID = wed)
}

# Step 3: Build edges wedding by wedding
edges_undirected <- map_dfr(unique(PublicDF$WeddingID), function(wed) {
  grp  <- PublicDF[PublicDF$WeddingID == wed, ]
  id_B <- grp$ID[grp$Role == "B"]
  id_G <- grp$ID[grp$Role == "G"]
  wit  <- grp[grepl("^W", grp$Role) & !is.na(grp$For) & grp$For != "N/A", ]

  bind_rows(
    # a) Bride to Groom
    make_pair(id_G, id_B, wed),
    # b) Witnesses, based on the For column
    map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(wit)), function(i) {
      w <- wit$ID[i]
      switch(wit$For[i],
        "Both"  = bind_rows(make_pair(w, id_B, wed), make_pair(w, id_G, wed)),
        "Bride" = make_pair(w, id_B, wed),
        "Groom" = make_pair(w, id_G, wed),
        NULL)
    })
  )
}) %>%
  filter(Source != Target)   # drop self-loops

# Step 4: Verify edge count - should return 2,141
nrow(edges_undirected)

# Step 5: Write to file
write_csv(edges_undirected, "edges_undirected.csv")
```


```{r build-edges-w-households}
# Build an extended edge list that adds enslaver household connections
# to the existing undirected edges. Enslaver nodes are identified by
# EnslaverID and linked to all enslaved participants in their household.
# Only enslavers associated with more than one participant are included,
# as single connections do not contribute to network formation.

# Step 1: Filter to EnslaverIDs associated with multiple participants
valid_enslavers <- PublicDF %>%
  filter(EnslaverID != "N/A") %>%
  group_by(EnslaverID) %>%
  filter(n_distinct(ID) > 1) %>%
  ungroup()

# Step 2: Create enslaver-to-participant edges
edges_household <- valid_enslavers %>%
  distinct(EnslaverID, ID) %>%
  rename(Source = EnslaverID,
         Target = ID)

# Step 3: Combine with undirected edges
edges_w_households <- bind_rows(
  edges_undirected %>% select(Source, Target),
  edges_household
)

# Step 4: Verify row count - should return 2,704
nrow(edges_w_households)

# Step 5: Write to file
write_csv(edges_w_households, "edges_w_households.csv")
```

```{r build-nodes-participants}
# Build a deduplicated participant nodes table
# Where Surname varies across appearances, non-blank entries are prioritized
# Name combines FirstName and Surname; FirstName only if Surname is blank

nodes_participants <- PublicDF %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  arrange(ID, is.na(Surname)) %>%      # non-NA surnames first
  summarise(
    FirstName = first(FirstName),
    Surname   = first(Surname),
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Name = if_else(is.na(Surname), FirstName, paste(FirstName, Surname))) %>%
  select(ID, Name)

# Verify
nrow(nodes_participants)
head(nodes_participants)

# Write to file
write_csv(nodes_participants, "nodes_participants.csv")
```

```{r build-nodes-enslavers}
# Build a deduplicated enslaver nodes table
# Limited to enslavers associated with 2 or more participants
# as only these contribute to network formation
# EnslaverName is entered as "Surname, First and Middle and Maternal Last Name"

nodes_enslavers <- PublicDF %>%
  filter(EnslaverID != "N/A") %>%
  group_by(EnslaverID) %>%
  filter(n_distinct(ID) > 1) %>%
  arrange(EnslaverID, desc(EnslaverName != "N/A")) %>%
  summarise(
    EnslaverName = first(EnslaverName),
    .groups      = "drop"
  ) %>%
  select(EnslaverID, EnslaverName)

# Verify - should return 215
nrow(nodes_enslavers)
head(nodes_enslavers)

# Write to file
write_csv(nodes_enslavers, "nodes_enslavers.csv")
```

```{r}
# Every edge endpoint should exist as a node
all_nodes <- c(nodes_participants$ID, nodes_enslavers$EnslaverID)
setdiff(unique(c(edges_w_households$Source, edges_w_households$Target)), all_nodes)
```
